newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PMP says leveraged to better economy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PMP says leveraged to better economy.

text.p: Publisher PMP Communications Ltd said on Wednesday it was well-placed to take advantage of any improvement in the Australian economy.
"The company is well leveraged to any improvement in Australian economic activity," PMP chairman Ken Cowley said in a statement accompanying its half year results.
PMP earlier said its net profit for the six months to December 31 fell 2.7 percent to A$30.5 million. The company maintained its interim dividend at 10.4 cents a share.

"During the period, much attention has been devoted to the integration of the Shomega business with our existing operations. Without dampening creativity, disciplines have been introduced to substantially reduce costs and improve the environment for management participation," Cowley said.
PMP acquired Shomega, a graphic arts and multi-media group, in June last year after launching a cash and scrip bid worth about A$176 million.

PMP said its bottom line was affected by goodwill amortisation of A$3.3 million relating to the Shomega acquisition and additional depreciation from printing plant commissioned mid-way through the previous first half.

"A soft retail environment and the lingering effects of last year's substantial increases in the cost of the major raw material, paper, put pressure on catalogue volumes and margins," the company said.
The company said its magazine printing revenues and earnings were stable despite pressure from recently negotiated long-term print contracts.
PMP's publishing division's half year earnings of A$20.1 million were A$1.5 million down on the previous corresponding period mainly due to higher paper costs.
"Advertising demand was soft in most Australian titles, and just over A$1 million in aggregate was expensed in relation to the launch of four new titles," PMP said.
At 2.55 p.m (0355 GMT), PMP shares were one cent firmer at A$3.65.
